diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $\rank(A) \leq 2$, therefore, a solution to $ch_A(x)$ is zero.

ch_A(x)&=\det(A-xI)\\&=\left[ \begin{array}{ccccc} -x & 0 & \cdots & 0 & a_{1} \\ 0 & -x & \cdots & 0 & a_{2} \\ \vdots & \vdots & & -x & a_{n-1} \\ a_1 & a_2 & \cdots & a_{n-1} & b-x \\ \end{array} \right]

issues.failure_explanation: For A=[[0,a^T],[a,b]] with a∈R^{n-1}, the actual eigenvalues are {b (mult n−2), (b±√(b²+4‖a‖²))/2}, not {0 (mult n−1), (b±√(b²+4‖a‖²))/2}. Zero is an eigenvalue only when b=0 or ‖a‖=0. The proof displays a matrix with −x on the diagonal (rows 2..n−1) and a-entries only in the last row/column; this is not A−xI (which has b−x on those diagonal entries and a-entries in the first row/column). The rank(A)≤2 claim is also false for n≥3 (e.g. a=(1,1),b=1 gives det A=−2≠0).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the lemma with the correct eigenvalue formula for the (n+1)×(n+1) block matrix [[0_n, v],[v^T, c]] (eigenvalues 0 with multiplicity n−1 and (c±√(c²+4‖v‖²))/2), with a valid proof via the 2×2 invariant subspace.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is a false mathematical statement. Theorem thm:cool cites this lemma to compute eigenvalues of a block matrix, but the block matrix in thm:cool has a different structure ([[0_n, v],[v^T, c]]) than the one in the lemma ([[0, a^T],[a, b]] with 1×1 zero), so the citation is invalid regardless of the lemma's own correctness.
issues.title: Lemma lm:rank2 states wrong eigenvalues and proves the characteristic polynomial of the wrong matrix
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained, well-known spectral computation for a block matrix; it does not require new architecture but does require replacing the stated result and its proof entirely.

issues.failure_explanation: The Gram matrix is [B^TB, γB^Ty; γy^TB, γ²‖x+y‖²]. The proof decomposes it as [B^TB,0;0,1]+[0,γB^Ty;γy^TB,γ²‖x+y‖²], whose sum has bottom-right entry 1+γ²‖x+y‖²≠γ²‖x+y‖². The correct split is [B^TB,0;0,γ²‖x+y‖²]+[0,γB^Ty;γy^TB,0]. Counterexample: B=[1], x=0, y=1, γ=1 gives [B,b]=[1,1] with κ=∞, but the stated bound evaluates to (3+√5)/2≈2.62. Additionally, the proof's substitution 'By assumption √(1+4‖B^Ty‖²/‖x+y‖²)≤ε' does not follow from the stated hypothesis ‖B^Ty‖/‖x+y‖≤(ε²−1)/4 for ε>√5.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must fix the matrix decomposition, re-derive valid Weyl-based bounds for σ_max and σ_min of [B,(x+y)γ], verify the resulting κ bound against counterexamples, and correct the hypothesis-to-implication gap in item 2. The stated closed-form bound is not recoverable by a local edit.
issues.overall_effect: The main condition-number-growth bound of Section 2 is false. Item 1's inequality does not hold in general, and item 2's derivation is built on the faulty item 1. The advertised application to QR analysis (Section 4) loses its general-theorem foundation.
issues.title: Theorem thm:cool is false; proof uses an incorrect matrix decomposition
issues.why_classification: The theorem statement is outright false (counterexample gives κ=∞ vs. finite bound). No one-line fix preserves the stated result; the proof architecture (decomposition + eigenvalue application) must be rebuilt, and it is unclear whether any bound of the stated form is true.

issues.failure_explanation: Evaluating the integral definition at α→0 gives Q^ma_M(0,β)=Γ(M,β²/2)/Γ(M), not Γ(M,β²)/Γ(M). The missing factor 1/2 in the upper incomplete gamma argument makes the stated special case inconsistent with the integral definition. Concretely, for M=1, β=1: the formula gives Γ(1,1)=e^{-1}≈0.368, but the integral gives Γ(1,1/2)=e^{-1/2}≈0.607.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the α=0 formula to Q^ma_M(0,β)=Γ(M,β²/2)/Γ(M). This is a one-character insertion (adding /2) that restores consistency with the integral definition and fixes cor:golden2.
issues.overall_effect: Corollary cor:golden2, which sets X=0 in thm:Malcum-Bessel, inherits the wrong value: P(‖Y‖≤ε)=1−Q^ma_{m/2}(0,ε/σ) uses the erroneous Γ(m/2,ε²/σ²) instead of Γ(m/2,ε²/(2σ²)), yielding an incorrect probability.
issues.title: Definition of Marcum-Q at α=0 has wrong incomplete-gamma argument
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single local correction (add factor 1/2); the integral definition and the general theorem thm:Malcum-Bessel are unaffected; all substantive claims survive with the corrected special-case value.

issues.failure_explanation: Z₁=‖P_Q Y‖ and Z₂=‖X+P_Q^⊥Y‖ are Euclidean norms, so Z₁²/σ²~χ²_n and Z₂²/σ²~χ'²_{m-n}(‖X‖²/σ²). The noncentral-F statistic is (Z₂²/(m−n))/(Z₁²/n). The event Z₁/Z₂≤ε₁/ε₂ is equivalent to (Z₂²/(m−n))/(Z₁²/n)≥nε₂²/((m−n)ε₁²). The proof and theorem use Z₁,Z₂ (not squared) in the ratio and the linear argument nε₂/((m−n)ε₁) (not nε₂²/((m−n)ε₁²)), giving an incorrect probability formula.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the F-argument nε₂/((m−n)ε₁) with nε₂²/((m−n)ε₁²) in both the theorem statement and the proof's derivation, and use Z₁², Z₂² in the F-statistic. This is a contained algebraic correction to the exponent.
issues.overall_effect: The probability statement in thm:noise-ls is numerically wrong for all non-trivial (ε₁,ε₂). Corollaries cor-main and cor:added-2, which invoke this F-bound, inherit the incorrect threshold.
issues.title: Theorem thm:noise-ls uses wrong argument in the noncentral-F probability (ε₂/ε₁ instead of ε₂²/ε₁²)
issues.why_classification: The structural approach (ratio of chi-squared → noncentral F) is correct, but the specific formula is wrong in a non-trivial way (missing squares). The fix is local but changes the numerical content of the bound and all downstream corollaries.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes κ([B,cγ])≤max{κ(B),‖B‖/|γ|,|γ|‖B†‖}·κ([Q,c]) (the second line). The first line, max{κ(B),‖B‖,‖B†‖}·κ([Q,cγ]), is a different expression: the max terms lack the γ-factors and the κ argument is [Q,cγ] rather than [Q,c]. These are not equal in general (e.g. take γ→0: first line →∞·κ([Q,cγ]) while second line →∞·κ([Q,c]) with different rates). The proof never derives the first line.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the first line (and the '&=' connecting it) from item 3, leaving only the proved bound max{κ(B),‖B‖/γ,γ‖B†‖}·κ([Q,c]). This preserves all valid content.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem statement contains a false identity. Downstream results that cite 'item 3' inherit ambiguity about which form is available.
issues.title: Theorem thm:min-max-cond item 3 asserts an unproved equality between two different bounds
issues.why_classification: The proof establishes one correct bound; the repair is to delete the unsupported first line. No substantive result is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem defines ‖r‖=min_z‖cγ−Bz‖ (residual of cγ). The Liesen formula κ([Q,cγ])=(α+√(α²−4γ²‖r_c‖²))/(2γ‖r_c‖) requires ‖r_c‖ to be the residual of c (not cγ). Since ‖r_{cγ}‖=γ‖r_c‖, the correct formula in terms of r_{cγ} is (α+√(α²−4‖r_{cγ}‖²))/(2‖r_{cγ}‖). The paper uses 4γ²‖r‖² with r=r_{cγ}, giving α²−4γ²‖r_{cγ}‖²=α²−4γ⁴‖r_c‖², which can be negative. Counterexample: B=[1;0], c=[0;1], γ=2 gives α=5, ‖r‖=2, α²−4γ²‖r‖²=25−64=−39<0, making the bound complex while κ([B,cγ])=2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either (a) change the residual definition to ‖r‖=min_z‖c−Bz‖ (residual of c) so the Liesen formula applies directly, or (b) replace the bound with κ(B)·(α+√(α²−4‖r‖²))/(2‖r‖) using r as the residual of cγ. Option (b) is the minimal formula correction.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem is undefined (complex-valued) for a range of valid inputs with γ≠1. Corollary cor-main, which applies this theorem, inherits the error for γ≠1. For γ=1 the formula coincides with the correct one, so cor:cond-ls is unaffected.
issues.title: Theorem lm:cond-ls misapplies the Liesen formula, yielding a complex/undefined bound for γ≠1
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local algebraic correction to the formula (removing the extraneous γ² inside the square root and the γ in the denominator), but it changes the theorem's statement and the residual's definition, and the current form is outright undefined for valid inputs.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume \( B \) is an \( m \times n \) full rank matrix \( (m > n) \) and \( X\in \mathrm{span}(B^{\perp}) \subset \mathbb{R}^m= \mathrm{span}(B^{\perp})\bigoplus \mathrm{span}(B) \) and \( Y \) is a random vector such that \( Y_i \) 's are i.i.d. with \( Y_i\sim N(0,\sigma^2) \).
The proof follows by recognizing that $\frac{1+\sqrt{1 - \|r\|_2^2}}{ \|r\|_2}$ is a decreasing function of $\|r\|_2$, and then applying Corollary \ref{cor:cond-ls} and Theorem \ref{thm:noise-ls}.

issues.failure_explanation: The vector q does not appear in the hypotheses and is never defined; the corollary asserts a bound on κ([B,q]) for an arbitrary, unspecified q. Moreover, the proof's decreasing-function argument yields, on the event ‖r‖≥1/√(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²), the bound κ(B)(√(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²)+ε₁/ε₂), not κ(B)·ε₁√(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²). These differ (e.g. ε₁=ε₂=1: 1+√2≈2.41 vs √2≈1.41), so the stated constant is not supported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define q explicitly (e.g. q=(X+Y)/‖X+Y‖ or the normalized noisy column), and replace the bound constant ε₁√(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²) with the correct expression √(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²)+ε₁/ε₂ (or a valid upper bound thereon) derived from the decreasing-function argument.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary is not a well-formed mathematical statement (q undefined) and the claimed bound is not the one derivable from the cited results. Corollary cor:added-2, which chains from cor-main, is affected.
issues.title: Corollary cor-main references an undefined vector q and states a bound that does not follow from the cited results
issues.why_classification: Two independent defects (undefined variable, wrong constant) require a contained but non-trivial repair: specifying the model for q and redoing the bound calculation. The overall strategy is salvageable.

issues.failure_explanation: ĈQ[:,i] denotes the i-th column of ĈQ, a single vector in R^m. The condition number κ of a single vector (viewed as an m×1 matrix) is undefined or trivially 1 (σ_max/σ_min with σ_min=0 for m>1), so κ(ĈQ[:,i]) is not a meaningful quantity. The intended object is κ(ĈQ[:,1:i]) (the matrix of the first i columns). Additionally, the variable w_i appears in the probability bound in the proof but is never defined in either the corollary statement or the proof setup. The statement also contains the syntactically broken phrase 'when the suppose a QR factorization algorithm' and uses ε₁, ε₂ (without subscripts i) in the F-argument while using ε_{1,i}, ε_{2,i} in the conclusion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace κ(ĈQ[:,i]) with κ(ĈQ[:,1:i]) throughout, define w_i (presumably the residual of a_i after projecting onto span(ĈQ[:,1:i−1])), and harmonize the ε-indexing between the F-bound and the conclusion. A complete proof sketch connecting each iteration to cor-main (once that is fixed) is also needed.
issues.overall_effect: The QR-algorithm corollary (the paper's final and most applied result) is not a well-defined statement: the key quantity κ(ĈQ[:,i]) is ill-defined, the auxiliary variable w_i is missing, and the parameter indices are inconsistent. The probabilistic guarantee for the accumulated condition number of ĈQ is therefore unsupported.
issues.title: Corollary cor:added-2 uses the condition number of a single column vector and references an undefined variable w_i
issues.why_classification: The fixes are local (correct subscript, define w_i, fix indices) but require clarifying the per-iteration model and ensuring the union-bound argument actually connects to the (corrected) upstream results. No new architecture is needed, but multiple coordinated edits are required.
